explanation.question_quote: Approximately 3 weeks ago, he had an anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction
explanation.sentence: The patient develops fever and sharp, positional chest pain three weeks after an anterior STEMI.
The sharp, positional pain and scratchy friction rub at the left sternal border point to acute pericarditis.
Widespread concave ST elevations with PR depressions further support pericarditis rather than a ventricular aneurysm.
The three-week delay is characteristic of Dressler’s syndrome, an autoimmune complication that occurs two to four weeks after myocardial infarction.
